exposure: early-life demographic factors (mode of birth, feeding type)
outcome: gut microbiome composition (bacterial diversity, taxonomic alterations)
gut microbiome function (lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, butanoate metabolism)
cohort: The study included 165 infants aged 0-12 months, comprising 120 cases with Rotavirus gastroenteritis and 45 healthy controls.
finding: Early-life demographic factors, particularly cesarean delivery and formula feeding, shaped gut microbiome composition and function, influencing Rotavirus gastroenteritis severity and leading to longer hospitalization for affected infants.
mod_finding: Cesarean-delivered infants, especially when formula-fed, exhibited more dysbiotic gut microbiomes and experienced 3.2-fold longer hospitalization due to RVGE compared to vaginally delivered, breastfed infants.
